newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nichiboshin says to post loss in 1st half.
newsitem.headline: Nichiboshin says to post loss in 1st half.

text.p: Japanese financial institution Nichiboshin Ltd said on Tuesday it expected to post a 28 billion yen to 29 billion yen parent current loss for the first half of 1996/97 ended September 30.
The non-bank added that it still expected to post a parent current profit of 16.8 billion yen for the full fiscal year.
A company official said the expected loss in the first half reflected its decision to make a loan loss provision worth 34.3 billion yen for a financially strapped affiliate.
The Nihon Keizai Shimbun daily reported on Tuesday that Nichiboshin's first-half net loss would be 40 billion yen.

The paper said that Nichiboshin has had difficulty in gaining consent from some of its creditors for a five-year restructuring programme worked out late last year and that it remains uncertain whether the non-bank will be able to see profits in the current fiscal year to next March.
The company official said that the report was speculative.

However, he confirmed that some of the more than 100 creditors had yet to agree with the non-bank on its restructuring programme and the company would continue to make efforts to gain approval in the second half.

Under the programme, creditors were asked to forgive a portion of their loans to Nichiboshin. Nichiboshin's borrowings from financial institutions total some 900 billion yen, of which the company wants lenders to forgive about 500 billion yen worth of loans in the five-year restructuring period.
In 1995/96, creditors were asked to forgive a total of 103.4 billion yen of loans to Nichiboshin, but 11.1 billion yen worth of loans were not forgiven by some creditors, the official said.
The non-bank earlier said it would post a special profit in the first half of 1996/97 if the 11.1 billion yen worth of the loans were forgiven in the first six months, he said.
